task.name: Spike: mechanical reviewer-reliability proxy — finding-fate rates from structured records
task.story_text:
## What

Spike: determine whether a mechanically observable proxy for reviewer
reliability exists — the downstream fate of the findings a reviewer raises —
so reviewer routing can gain a quality-adjacent signal without the unavailable
ground truth that keeps LLM-judged review "quality" in advisory-only territory
(ADR-0006 clause 3, bucket C).

"Was this P1 good?" is mushy and stays bucket C. But a narrower question may
be coordinator-observable and therefore bucket B (routing-safe after
aggregation): after a reviewer raises a finding, was it addressed in-cycle,
dismissed by the dev, contradicted by a later reviewer, or did it survive
subsequent review? That is an event over structured records, not a judgment —
provided the downstream events are themselves structured.

## What has changed since filing

The finding registry the coordinator now maintains across review cycles
records a disposition per finding, and real audits already carry values like
fixed, net-new, corroborated-new, and ac-blocking. Part of the structured
event stream this spike was going to ask for already exists in production
data. The open question is no longer "could such events exist" but "do the
recorded dispositions, joined with cycle-over-cycle finding tracking and
verdicts, cover the four fate classes — and where they don't, what is the
smallest structured event that closes the gap."

Relationship to shipped work: the reviewer-value signal that landed for
code-review routing measures uniqueness — did this reviewer surface blocking
findings no peer did. Fate is orthogonal: what happened to a finding after it
was raised. A reviewer can be unique and consistently dismissed, or
unoriginal and consistently confirmed.

## Acceptance criteria (spike deliverables)

- A written determination for each fate class — addressed, dismissed,
  contradicted, survived — stating whether it is derivable from records the
  coordinator already writes; each class either names its derivation or names
  the smallest structured event that would have to be added. A class that can
  only be inferred from prose is reported as out of scope, not approximated.
- A validating POC computes per-reviewer fate rates over the existing audit
  corpus and its output is included in the spike result: rates with sample
  counts per reviewer, with the clause-2 admissibility gates (sample floor,
  recency weighting, taint exclusion) applied, and the excluded-sample counts
  shown.
- The spike ends with an explicit adoption decision: admit the proxy as a
  bucket-B routing signal folding into the existing mechanical reviewer-signal
  family, or record why it stays out. The decision states the recording cost
  of any new event it requires and how the signal would be tested.

## Example

The shape the POC should produce, sufficient to decide on:

```
Finding-fate proxy — corpus: all admissible story audits

reviewer          findings   addressed  dismissed  contradicted  survived   n(excl. tainted)
reviewer-A             168         71%         6%            2%       21%        219
reviewer-B              36         84%         3%            0%       13%         28
reviewer-C               8         25%        50%           12%       13%        118
...

underivable classes: <none | list, each with the missing structured event>
```

## Scope boundary

Mechanical proxy only. Open-ended quality/goodness/helpfulness scoring without
structured corroboration stays advisory (clause 3 bucket C) and is explicitly
out of scope — that is the unwinnable-target trap this spike exists to avoid.

## References

- ADR-0006 clause 3 (bucket taxonomy), clause 2 (admissibility), clause 4
  (taint exclusion)
- #1443 (mechanical reviewer value signals), #2156 (uniqueness signal for
  code-review routing, shipped), #1391 (routing-decision explainability)

findings.description: The module defines the frozenset _ADJACENT_CONTRADICTION_MARKERS containing gate_contradicted and downgraded, but no code path reads it — the two adjacent markers are matched by separate inline string comparisons in analyze_records instead.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 maps gate_contradicted and downgraded into the contradicted fate, although neither establishes the specified event: contradiction by a later reviewer. gate_contradicted is assigned by coordinator/review_phase.py from the same-cycle gate result, while downgraded in finding_classifier.py records only a P1-to-P2 severity change and retains no later reviewer's identity. Publishing either as the contradicted rate would approximate an underivable class, contrary to the first acceptance criterion.
  Suggestion: Mark later-reviewer contradiction as underivable. Name a structured relation keyed by finding ID, cycle, and contradicting reviewer as the missing event. Gate contradictions and severity downgrades may be reported separately as adjacent observations, but not in the required contradicted-rate column.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 does not correctly apply the code-review signal's clause-2 gate. It selects assignment.reviewer_value_min_runs, which is the plan-review floor used at assignment.py:4018; code-review routing uses assignment.code_review_value_min_runs at assignment.py:4093. It also feeds per-finding one-hot values directly to _weighted_rate, whose ordered ring and decay positions represent run observations. Multiple findings from one run would receive different recency weights and could satisfy the min_runs floor as though they were independent runs.
  Suggestion: Use code_review_value_min_runs and define the admissibility population in review-run observations. Apply recency by run so findings from the same audit share the same age, while reporting raw finding counts separately. If a per-finding floor is desired instead, introduce and document a distinct floor rather than labeling it ADR-0006 min_runs.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 1 (single-reporter attribution) is carried, not retired: FindingRecord has exactly one reporter field (coordinator/state.py:196), so a corroborated_new finding raised independently by two reviewers credits only one. The plan's mitigation is disclosure in the output/doc plus naming a structured multi-reporter event as recording cost — that limits the fate rates' meaning but does not block any AC, since the ACs require rates plus stated limits, not unbiased attribution.
  Suggestion: Have the POC emit the corroborated_new share of the sample per reviewer alongside the fate columns, so the reader can size the attribution bias rather than only being told it exists.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 reuses _recency_params and _weighted_rate — private helpers of model_profiles_read_model. They are duck-typed and importable, and reviewer_value already routes through _weighted_rate, so this works; but a spike-only package importing another module's underscore-prefixed API is a seam that will need a public entry point if the proxy is ever admitted to production routing.
  Suggestion: Note this in the Step 5 adoption path's cost line (promote to a public helper on admission), so the decision does not read as zero-integration-cost.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 says 'compute per-reviewer fate counts from audit finding_registry records', but audit.py serializes two distinct registries: finding_registry (code review, has reporter, audit.py:1164) and plan_finding_registry (plan review, audit.py:993 — no reporter and a narrower Disposition of unresolved/fixed/new). The plan-side registry cannot support per-reviewer attribution at all.
  Suggestion: State in Step 1 that the POC reads only the code-review finding_registry, and record in the Step 4 determination that plan-review findings are out of the corpus because no reporter is serialized for them.

finding_registry.description: The module defines the frozenset _ADJACENT_CONTRADICTION_MARKERS containing gate_contradicted and downgraded, but no code path reads it — the two adjacent markers are matched by separate inline string comparisons in analyze_records instead.

The spike record presents addressed and survived as two independent per-reviewer rates, but because the derivable set contains exactly those two fates, each run's survived share is always one minus its addressed share, so the two published columns carry a single degree of freedom rather than two.

The explanatory sentence about addressed and survived being complements was inserted inside the fenced block introduced as what the POC reported on a specific date, but render() emits only the single recency-weighted-means line in that position, so the block presented as a transcript now contains a line the program never printed.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
